events.name: load_libraries_entry
events.condition: Observed when local Java/Kotlin source contains an invocation or declaration substring matching "loadLibraries(". This alone does not establish that the method executed or attempted to load a native library.

events.name: native_load_attempt
events.condition: Observed when a matching Java/Kotlin native-library loading call appears on a feasible path. Its success predicate is not satisfied merely by observing the call; success requires runtime evidence that the requested library was found and mapped.

events.name: native_link_failure_reported
events.condition: Observed when source references java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError. The finding predicate is satisfied only if the detector or runtime report associates an UnsatisfiedLinkError with org.xbmc.kodi.NativeLoader.loadLibraries and the reported missing-library detail; a source reference or catch block alone does not satisfy that predicate.

detector_semantics.claim: A native-link/load failure was reported in the context of org.xbmc.kodi.NativeLoader.loadLibraries, with the representative detail "dlopen failed: library 'libkodi.so' not found."
predicates: Reported detail identifies libkodi.so as not found.
limitations: No detector-rule implementation or NativeLinkError CrySL source was available to establish whether these predicates are exact matching conditions, normalized fields, or presentation-only text.
The report does not identify the actual native-loading call site, library-name argument, class loader, APK split, ABI, linker namespace, or execution path.
The report demonstrates neither a general typestate violation nor a security property.

documented_behavior: For the actual API evidenced by the finding, Android documents java.lang.UnsatisfiedLinkError as occurring when the VM cannot find an appropriate native-language definition for a native method.

Android documents System.loadLibrary(String) as loading a library by logical name from a system library location and as capable of throwing UnsatisfiedLinkError when the name contains a path, the library is not statically linked with the VM, or the host cannot map it to a native library image.
The JDK documentation describes the same general loading model and exception category.
preconditions: For System.loadLibrary(String), the logical library name must not include a platform-specific prefix, filename extension, or path.
A successful runtime load additionally depends on implementation-specific native-library lookup and host mapping behavior.
The reported libkodi.so message requires runtime evidence; it cannot be established solely from a source-level load call.
unknowns: No documented behavior was found for an API type named NativeLinkError in the stated CrySL corpus.
It is unknown whether the named specification is a local synthetic detector label, a missing corpus rule, or an incorrectly named rule.
It is unknown which Java/Android loading API, if any, is called by NativeLoader.loadLibraries.
